title: Which runtime areas are per thread, and why Metaspace replaced PermGen

questions.stem: Which of the JVM's runtime data areas does every thread get its own copy of?

options.text: The heap, the Java stack and the PC register.
options.says: The heap is shared by all threads and managed by the garbage collector; only the stack and the PC register are per thread in this list.

options.text: The method area, the PC register and the native method stack.
options.says: The method area is shared by all threads; only the Java stack, PC register and native method stack are per thread.

options.text: The Java stack, the PC register and the native method stack.
options.says: These three hold one thread's frames, its current instruction and its native calls, while the heap and the method area are shared.

questions.stem: Why did Java 8 replace PermGen with Metaspace for class metadata?

options.text: Metadata moved to native memory that grows on demand, out of a fixed-size heap area.
options.says: PermGen's fixed maximum caused OutOfMemoryError: PermGen space in class-heavy applications; Metaspace grows dynamically and is bounded only if MaxMetaspaceSize is set.

options.text: Metadata moved to the old generation of the heap, which full collections can shrink.
options.says: Metaspace is not in the heap at all: the page puts class metadata in native memory.

options.text: Metadata moved to a fixed-size native area whose size is set once at start.
options.says: Metaspace grows on demand; a fixed size was PermGen's problem, not its replacement.
